requirements.requirement: node1 becomes the DNS resolver for the shared private network, listening/serving scoped to it
requirements.summary: VyOS service dns forwarding configured with listen-address 10.100.10.10 and allow-from 10.100.10.0/24; committed and saved. pdns-recursor confirmed active and listening on 10.100.10.10:53 both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: node1 answers inventory.internal with node2's address on the shared network
requirements.summary: authoritative-domain inventory.internal record a @ -> 10.100.10.11 (node2's confirmed IP) was set and committed; dig confirms this both pre- and post-reboot, and resolvectl on node2/node3 independently confirms the same result.

requirements.requirement: node1 forwards all other queries upstream
requirements.summary: name-server 1.1.1.1 and 9.9.9.9 configured as forwarders; dig for example.com resolves to real public IPs both before and after node1's reboot.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 configured to resolve DNS through node1
requirements.summary: A systemd-networkd drop-in (DNS=10.100.10.10, UseDNS=no) was applied on both nodes; resolvectl shows current DNS server 10.100.10.10 with inventory.internal and example.com resolving correctly, confirmed again after each node's own reboot.

overall_summary: node1 was configured as an authoritative-plus-forwarding DNS resolver scoped to the 10.100.10.0/24 network, answering inventory.internal with node2's address and forwarding everything else upstream. node2 and node3 were both switched to use node1 as DNS server via a persistent systemd-networkd override. All functional claims are backed by direct dig/resolvectl evidence, re-verified after each node's individual reboot with changed boot IDs consistent with fixed lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary mutations or hygiene issues found.
limitations: The provider-wide restart-evidence protocol, while not part of the public task contract, was executed thoroughly and cross-checks consistently against fixed snapshots.
No negative test confirming the allow-from restriction blocks non-LAN clients was captured; a minor gap in the scoping proof.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands map clearly to task outcomes or the restart-evidence protocol: the VyOS dns-forwarding commit/save on node1, the systemd-networkd DNS drop-ins on node2/node3, and the three sequential reboots. No abandoned experiments or residue, no failed services, no package damage, and DNS exposure is correctly scoped. Numerous 'not valid' CLI probes were read-only syntax discovery with no commit and did not mutate persisted state.
